scope.current_boundary: Determine velocity using the gradient of a displacement-time graph and acceleration using the gradient of a velocity-time graph. Do not teach area under a velocity-time graph or construct full motion graphs.
scope.previous_boundary_used: Reading displacement-time and velocity-time graphs, including axes, signs, stationary motion, direction, constant velocity and changing motion.
scope.next_boundary_checked: Area and constructing motion graphs, including signed area under velocity-time graphs and graph construction.

question_patterns_used.name: Graph interpretation
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: Axis-first identification, sign interpretation, tangent method and straight-line versus curved-gradient decisions.

question_patterns_used.name: Direct calculation
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: Two fully worked signed-gradient calculations with units and checks.

question_patterns_used.name: Comparison
question_patterns_used.lesson_response: Explicit comparison of what gradient means for the two graph types and of average against instantaneous gradient.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped lesson graph sketch with a negative velocity-time gradient and zero crossing.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Recognise constant negative acceleration as a straight negative-slope line.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Read start, zero-velocity and final negative-velocity points while preserving sign.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Stopping at zero velocity or treating a negative velocity as a negative speed.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped sketch demand for uniform deceleration from positive velocity to rest.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Sketch an appropriate velocity-time trend from verbal motion information.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Use constant rate of velocity change to choose a straight line and use the endpoint condition correctly.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Drawing a curve for constant acceleration.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped calculation of acceleration from two points on a straight velocity-time graph.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Read two values, find change in velocity and divide by elapsed time.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Identify the graph axis, use a large interval and retain velocity units.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Using velocity divided by time instead of the change in velocity divided by time.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped constant-acceleration graph-gradient calculation in a return-motion context.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Extract acceleration from a velocity-time graph while respecting direction.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Treat the signed graph gradient as acceleration before considering later motion stages.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Dropping the sign or confusing velocity with acceleration.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped multi-stage application beginning with acceleration from a straight velocity-time graph.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Isolate the graph-gradient calculation before later dynamics calculations.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Choose widely separated points on one straight segment, then calculate signed gradient.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Using a changing portion of a graph as if it had one constant gradient.

questions_visited.why_selected: Mapped instantaneous acceleration calculation from a curved velocity-time graph.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Draw a tangent at a stated time and find its gradient.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Use points on the tangent, not distant points on the curve.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Using a secant line and calling its average gradient instantaneous acceleration.

questions_visited.why_selected: Topic-relevant tangent-gradient calculation for instantaneous speed from a curved distance-time graph.
questions_visited.assessed_demand: Use a tangent and its gradient rather than a long secant line.
questions_visited.reasoning_route: Recognise that gradient units identify speed or velocity from a distance/displacement-time graph.
questions_visited.misconception_or_distractor: Reading a y-value as a speed or calculating a gradient from the curve rather than tangent.
